summary: Best complementary source found is AHRQ’s SOPS Hospital Survey 2.0 instrument and its voluntary hospital benchmark. The instrument is public and directly covers teamwork, communication, reporting, staffing, and handoffs. Benchmark results are national voluntary-submitter aggregates, not local observations of RWJUH or Saint Peter’s. No publicly downloadable New Brunswick or Middlesex workflow narratives or facility-level survey results were verified in this bounded search. A draft interview and process-map guide is included as a next step; it does not represent collected local evidence.

sources.title: SOPS Hospital Survey 2.0, survey items, and user guide
sources.publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
sources.geography: United States; instrument intended for hospitals and used internationally, but international translation/use may require permission
sources.period: Version 2.0 released 2019; retain the version and local administration dates if collected
sources.grain: Instrument items and composite measures; not local response records
useful_fields: Supervisor/Manager/Clinical Leader Support for Patient Safety (3 items)
Hospital Management Support for Patient Safety (3 items)
observed_facts: AHRQ provides English and Spanish survey forms, an item/composite reference, and a user guide on its official page.
AHRQ says the survey assesses provider and staff perceptions; the tool is an instrument, not evidence of responses at either New Brunswick hospital.
The FAQ states AHRQ SOPS surveys and related materials are free for public use in the United States.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Download the English Version 2.0 survey, item/composite reference, and user guide from the linked AHRQ page. Preserve the version, download date, source URL, and document hashes. For a draft journey guide, map one bounded journey (for example, ED arrival through inpatient admission or inter-unit transfer) by stage; ask role-specific prompts about decision authority, information handed off, required fields, escalation triggers, exceptions, workarounds, and what happens when a handoff is incomplete. Label all proposed answers as questions until authorized local collection occurs.
limitations: Survey responses would measure staff perceptions and reported culture, not directly establish actual workflow frequency or clinical outcomes.
Do not present the national database benchmark as a New Brunswick hospital score.
Original interviews or observations require an agreed consent and research process; no interviews are scheduled or implied here.
AHRQ notes international users must contact the program for permission to translate and use the instrument outside the United States.

sources.title: SOPS Hospital Database: 2024 Hospital 2.0 report and supplemental results
sources.publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
sources.period: 2024 report database; AHRQ dashboard describes collection windows as 2022-08-01 through 2024-06-30 for database year 2024
sources.grain: Published aggregate results by hospital and respondent characteristics; underlying research files require an application
useful_fields: Percent-positive results for survey items and composite measures
observed_facts: AHRQ reports 445 hospitals and more than 280,000 staff/providers in the 2024 Hospital 2.0 database report.
The 2024 workplace-safety supplemental results include 94 hospitals and 61,767 staff/providers.
AHRQ explicitly says participation is voluntary and the database is not representative of all U.S. hospitals.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Download the 2024 report, executive summary, and appendixes linked on the AHRQ database page. Use the appendixes to select only relevant measure and respondent/hospital strata for a clearly labeled external benchmark. The AHRQ data tool also links an accessible XLSX export; retain its displayed database year and definitions. If local hospital-identifiable data are essential, first determine whether each hospital submitted data, then follow AHRQ’s formal request route; this requires application, confidentiality terms, AHRQ approval, and each submitting hospital’s written authorization.
limitations: This source does not establish that RWJUH CCN 310038 or Saint Peter’s CCN 310070 participated.
Published voluntary-submitter aggregates may differ in hospital mix and respondent roles from the target facilities.

Underlying de-identified respondent data require a research abstract and signed data release agreement; hospital-identifiable data require additional approval and hospital authorization. No agreement is accepted or requested in this task.

sources.title: AHRQ National Healthcare Safety Dashboard: SOPS Hospital Patient Safety Culture view
sources.publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ), National Action Alliance for Patient and Workforce Safety
sources.geography: United States; voluntary SOPS Hospital 2.0 database participants
sources.period: Database years 2021, 2022, and 2024; dashboard specifies the collection windows for each year
sources.grain: Unweighted hospital-level percent-positive scores by SOPS culture measure, with dashboard filters; accessible XLSX export is linked on the page
useful_fields: Supervisor/Manager/Clinical Leader Support for Patient Safety
Hospital Management Support for Patient Safety
observed_facts: The dashboard defines scores as unweighted average hospital-level percent-positive responses.
It describes 2024 collection as August 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024; 2022 as November 1, 2020 through July 31, 2022; and 2021 as November 1, 2018 through October 31, 2020.
The dashboard warns that the sample is voluntary and not nationally representative; pandemic conditions may have affected results.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Open the SOPS view, record filters and definitions, and download the linked accessible XLSX file. Verify the export’s columns and row grain before loading; preserve dashboard URL, retrieval date, and database year. Use as an external comparison range only, not as a local calibration target.
limitations: The XLSX is a public dashboard export, not unrestricted respondent-level microdata.
Results are voluntary-submitter aggregates and should not be extrapolated to either named hospital or Middlesex County.
Dashboard measures perceptions; they do not encode local exception rules, authority boundaries, or observed handoff sequences.

missing_inputs: No verified public local dataset was found in this search for role-by-workflow-stage rules, handoff narratives, workarounds, or safety-culture responses at RWJUH or Saint Peter’s.
No verified direct downloadable facility-level SOPS score for either CCN was found. Check the public dashboard’s facility filters and confirm identity coverage before asserting absence or presence.
A local process-map requires an explicitly selected journey and authorized institutional collection of policies, de-identified workflow artifacts, or consented interviews/observations.
Need to preserve policy effective dates, survey administration dates, role, unit/context, and conflicting accounts in any local collection.
simulation_use: Use SOPS 2.0 as a candidate vocabulary and survey-scale schema for synthetic culture variables, while tagging all benchmark values as external voluntary-database aggregates. It can inform candidate dimensions such as communication openness and handoff information exchange, but cannot calibrate local behavior. For the next bounded collection, select one journey and create a draft role-specific map/interview guide with rows for stage, actor/role, decision authority, input information, handoff recipient, rule, exception/escalation, workaround, timing/context, evidence type, and unresolved disagreement. Keep uncollected answers blank; do not infer local rules from the national instrument.
limitations: Research was limited to two searches and four official primary-source page opens; discovery is not acquisition.
Only AHRQ primary sources were inspected. No local institution-specific workflow narratives were verified.
Source listings and suggested downloads are candidates for independent verification and acquisition; no dataset was acquired in this response.
The AHRQ public instrument and aggregate reports do not satisfy the required local role × workflow stage × rule/exception/theme × context grain.
